actions.text: The shift-based reduction made scalar_mul and msm only 0.2% cheaper and decode 0.9% more expensive, well short of the 1% minimum. I'll revert it.

actions.diff:
--- a/secp256r1/src/field.rs
+++ b/secp256r1/src/field.rs
@@ -383,3 +383,1 @@
-    // MODULUS[0] = 2^64 - 1 and MODULUS[1] = 2^32 - 1, so adding
-    // m * MODULUS[0..2] to the low words is the same as adding m * 2^96.
-    let (r1, carry) = shl32_add(r1, r0);
+    let (r1, carry) = mac(r1, r0, MODULUS[1], r0);

--- a/secp256r1/src/field.rs
+++ b/secp256r1/src/field.rs
@@ -421,9 +0,0 @@
-/// Returns `a + b * 2^32` as a low word and a carry word, which equals
-/// `mac(a, b, MODULUS[1], b)`.
-#[inline(always)]
-fn shl32_add(a: u64, b: u64) -> (u64, u64) {
-    let (low, overflow) = a.overflowing_add(b << 32);
-    (low, (b >> 32) + u64::from(overflow))
-}
-

actions.reason: The one change I measured missed the 1% minimum. In the Montgomery reduction in secp256r1/src/field.rs, I replaced the four multiplies by MODULUS[1] (2^32 - 1, plus the added low word) with an equivalent shift-and-add. Outputs were identical, but the ratios were msm_ir 0.9980, scalar_mul_ir 0.9979 and decode_ir 1.0090 (worse), against the 0.9900 needed. I reverted it, so the tree is back to the parent. The field multiply is already close to what the compiler can do. From rough field-operation counts, the other ideas would also likely fall short: other window widths in the msm loop, a different doubling formula, and other mixed-addition variants. I did not measure them. Stopping without a candidate rather than spending the remaining budget on guesses.

journal.text:
I tried one change in the Montgomery reduction in secp256r1/src/field.rs. The four multiplies by MODULUS[1], which is 2^32 - 1, plus the added low word, became an equivalent shift-and-add. I read group.rs and field.rs around the reduction and the mul/square paths first.

The candidate built and outputs were identical to the parent. msm_ir went from 188568597 to 188188253, ratio 0.9980. scalar_mul_ir went from 258848011 to 258304322, ratio 0.9979. decode_ir got worse, 145913159 to 147227112, ratio 1.0090. The gate needs 0.9900, so it was rejected as no_improvement. I reverted the edits and submitted nothing.

The multiply by MODULUS[1] is not a cost that matters here. The compiler likely already lowers it well, and a shift-and-add saves almost nothing. The reduction structure may hold more than its constants.

Next I will look at the msm path in group.rs, at wnaf width and batch_normalize, before touching field arithmetic again. I also want to know why decode_ir moved up.
